intent.raw: Create a research strategy for academic and market references for UX good practices, mixing cognitive science, neuroscience, tested market practices, so we can formulate a validator and tester using Playwright to test and produce evidence of finished frontend interfaces.
intent.objective: Plan a governed multi-lane research route that turns UX references into evidence cards, validator taxonomy, Playwright test harness requirements, calibration fixtures, and implementation handoff artifacts.
intent.operator_sentence: Use dispatch-spec to define a multi-lane UX evidence research route, then hand off to research and Playwright validator implementation only after reference cards and calibration fixtures exist.

route_menu.context_hint: The selected route separates source harvest, claim mapping, validator design, Playwright harness design, calibration, and implementation handoff.

items.label: Multi-lane evidence route
items.description: Research accessibility standards, cognitive science, neuroscience/perception, market practices, and browser-testing documentation in parallel before synthesis.

items.label: Standards first
items.description: Start with WCAG, ARIA, and Playwright evidence contracts, then add cognitive and market-practice overlays.

items.label: Fixture first
items.description: Design known-good and known-bad UI fixtures before broad reference harvest.

technique_overlays.trigger: External UX claims must be normalized before they become validator rules.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Every imported reference has a source URL, narrow claim, evidence strength, UI scope, automation candidate, contraindication, and freshness rule.

technique_overlays.trigger: Finished frontend interfaces need repeatable browser evidence, not prose-only review.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Playwright evidence names screenshots, traces, accessibility output, ARIA snapshots, DOM measurements, viewport matrix, and result report paths.

subagent_strategy.trigger: The research target crosses standards, cognitive science, neuroscience/perception, market practice, and browser automation evidence.
subagent_strategy.explanation: Parallel role-bound researchers reduce source bias and keep hard validator gates separate from softer UX risk prompts.
context: UX validation spans deterministic browser behavior, standards conformance, empirical/human-factor research, market heuristics, and subjective user evidence.
The strategy must avoid turning neuroscience or market heuristics into overconfident automated rules.

roles.purpose: Harvest WCAG, ARIA, accessibility-testing, keyboard, focus, and semantic UI evidence.
roles.owns: hard accessibility gates; automated accessibility report requirements

roles.purpose: Harvest cognitive load, working memory, decision complexity, motor-control, and workload evidence.
roles.owns: cognitive-load proxy map; human-study residue lane

roles.purpose: Harvest visual search, attention, salience, grouping, motion sensitivity, and perception evidence.
roles.owns: attention-risk proxy map; visual hierarchy review prompts

roles.purpose: Harvest tested practitioner and domain-specific UX practices from credible market sources.
roles.owns: market-practice evidence cards; domain-specific rule pack candidates

roles.purpose: Translate validated claims into browser probes, evidence receipts, fixtures, screenshots, traces, and measurement artifacts.
roles.owns: Playwright evidence contract; fixture calibration plan

subagent_strategy.permission_prompt: Run delegated UX evidence research agents before creating the validator implementation work-pack?

boundaries.contract: External sources are harvested into evidence cards with source URL, claim, evidence strength, contraindications, and freshness rule.
Invoke may convert the passed research artifacts into an implementation work-pack, but Dispatch Spec remains route-shape validation only.
Browser tests return structured evidence receipts with run metadata, screenshots, trace/video, accessibility output, DOM/ARIA snapshots, measurements, and residue.

authority.validation: dispatch-spec for route shape; future ux validator for interface checks

state_namespaces.write_policy: Research strategy and dispatch documents may be added under formulae/dispatch-spec/development only for this route.
Browser evidence should be written under output/playwright/ux-validator or a route-specific evidence directory.
Store summaries and links, not copied full external documents.

promotion_splits.rule: requires synthesis review before becoming executable hard gates.
requires owning capability review before any inventory, ontology, glossary, sigil, or spell promotion.

steps.name: Select UX evidence research route
stop_conditions: Block if the route collapses research, validator implementation, and promotion into one step.
Ask before executing delegated research agents.

steps.name: Harvest academic, standards, neuroscience, market, and tooling references

inputs.ref: WCAG, Playwright, axe-core, Nielsen Norman Group, Baymard, GOV.UK, cognitive-science and neuroscience literature

convergence_criteria: Each lane returns at least five candidate references or explicitly records scarcity.
Each claim distinguishes deterministic browser-check candidates from human-review or user-study candidates.
Each external claim includes source URL, source type, evidence strength, contraindications, and freshness rule.
Neuroscience and cognitive-science claims are translated conservatively into UI proxies.
stop_conditions: Block any source claim without a stable citation or access note.
Flag market-practice claims that are domain-specific but presented as universal.
Flag academic claims that cannot be operationalized or require human-study evidence.

steps.name: Map references into UX evidence claims and proxy limits
convergence_criteria: Claims are grouped as hard_gate, soft_flag, screenshot_review, human_study, or not_automatable.
Every claim names what Playwright can observe and what remains outside browser automation.
Each high-level UX principle decomposes into narrow testable or reviewable claims.
stop_conditions: Block if a cognitive or neuroscience claim is mapped directly to a hard browser gate without a proxy justification.

steps.name: Derive validator taxonomy and rule candidates
convergence_criteria: The taxonomy separates smoke, accessibility, layout integrity, interaction flow, cognitive/attention risk, domain-practice, and human-evidence layers.
Hard gates are deterministic or standards-backed.
Soft flags preserve evidence strength and review owner.
Each layer names evidence artifacts and failure interpretation.
stop_conditions: Block if subjective UX claims are scored as deterministic pass/fail without human evidence.

steps.name: Define Playwright evidence harness contract
convergence_criteria: The harness contract names viewport matrix, scenario format, screenshot policy, trace/video policy, accessibility scan policy, DOM/ARIA snapshot policy, measurement JSON, and residue report.
The contract includes blocked, flag, and pass statuses.
The contract names exact output roots for browser evidence.
stop_conditions: Block if Playwright evidence paths are not concrete.
Flag if the harness cannot distinguish hard gates from soft UX risk prompts.

steps.name: Calibrate validator with known-good and known-bad fixtures
convergence_criteria: At least one good fixture and five bad fixtures cover accessibility, layout, flow, cognitive-risk, and false-positive cases.
Hard gates catch deterministic failures.
Soft flags are explainable and reference their evidence card.
Screenshots and JSON evidence are written to the declared output root.
stop_conditions: Block if calibration cannot reproduce known failures.
Flag rules that generate ambiguous or high-noise soft findings.

steps.name: Prepare implementation handoff for validator and tester
convergence_criteria: Operator approves whether the next route is research execution, validator spec, fixture design, or implementation.
Residue separates missing sources, subjective claims, fixture gaps, and future domain packs.
stop_conditions: Ask the operator before implementation starts.
Block if evidence cards or fixture plan are missing.

gates.condition: Every imported UX claim must cite a source URL, source type, evidence strength, contraindication, and freshness rule.
The route must distinguish Playwright-observable failures from review-only or human-study claims.
The future tester must produce screenshots, traces or videos, accessibility output, DOM or ARIA snapshots, measurement JSON, console or network summaries, and residue.
Validator rules must pass known-good and known-bad fixture calibration before being treated as hard gates.
Execution evidence must not promote inventory, ontology, glossary, sigil, or spell knowledge without owner review.
The operator chooses the next route before research execution, fixture work, or validator implementation begins.

promotion_guardrails: Do not treat Playwright screenshots as proof of subjective UX quality.
Do not convert neuroscience or cognitive-science claims into hard gates without conservative UI proxies and fixture calibration.
Do not treat market-practice evidence as universal outside its domain without product-context review.
Do not promote inventory, ontology, glossary, sigil, or spell knowledge from execution evidence without owner review.
Do not modify future validator source until the operator approves the implementation route.
